_note: Pension tax relief rules for tools/build-pension-relief-pages.js, quoted from GOV.UK. The extra relief higher rate taxpayers claim follows the income tax bands in the UK tax files (data/tax/gb), so only these rules live here.
note: 'You can get tax relief on private pension contributions worth up to 100% of your annual earnings.' Relief at source: 'your pension provider claims tax relief from the government at the basic 20% rate and adds it to your pension pot'. 'If your rate of Income Tax in Scotland is 19% your pension provider will claim tax relief for you at a rate of 20%. You do not need to pay the difference.' Non-taxpayers: relief at 20% 'up to either: 80% of your earnings in that year [or] £2,880 if you have no earnings in that year'. England, Wales or Northern Ireland: claim '20% up to the amount of any income you have paid 40% tax on' and '25% up to the amount of any income you have paid 45% tax on'. Scotland: '1% ... 21% ... 22% ... 42% ... 25% ... 45% ... 28% ... 48%'. Example: 'You earn £60,270 ... You can claim an extra 20% tax relief on £10,000 (the same amount you paid 40% tax on)'. Annual allowance: 'This is £60,000 this tax year'; tapered if 'threshold income is over £200,000' and 'adjusted income is over £260,000'.
